Verify the star rating is visible in the product info panel
Failed ▼
# Action Expected / Result Status
#01 Verify visible: Star rating widget The star rating widget should be visible in the product info panel alongside the SKU
⚠ Errorlocator.waitFor: Timeout 15000ms exceeded. Call log: [2m - waiting for locator('#pdp-info-panel').locator('Star rating widget').first()[22m
🔍 Source HTML — element NOT FOUND · <body> verify_visible click to zoom
🔍 Root Cause
[B] TEST SELECTOR ISSUE — The test is using a plain text string 'Star rating widget' as a Playwright locator, which is not a valid CSS selector, XPath, or stable attribute selector. Additionally, the live page HTML provided shows only <body></body>, which strongly indicates the page either failed to load or the snapshot was captured before the DOM rendered; however, the primary issue is the completely invalid locator string that would never match any real DOM element. Playwright interprets 'Star rating widget' as a CSS selector, which is invalid and will always time out.
❌ Problematic Code
selector: 'Star rating widget'
# Used as: locator('#pdp-info-panel').locator('Star rating widget').first()
# 'Star rating widget' is not a valid CSS selector, XPath, or attribute value.
✅ Fixed Code
# Option 1 — target star rating by common Magento rating widget attributes/classes:
selector: '[data-bind*="rating"], .rating-summary, .product-reviews-summary .rating-result'

# Option 2 — if using aria attributes:
selector: '[aria-label*="rating"], [role="img"][class*="rating"]'

# Option 3 — XPath text/class based approach:
selector: '//div[@id="pdp-info-panel"]//*[contains(@class,"rating")]'

# Recommended YAML fix (replace the broken selector line):
- action: verify_visible
  selector: '#pdp-info-panel .rating-summary'
  description: Verify the star rating is visible in the product info panel
📋 What To Do
  • **Inspect the live PDP HTML** in a browser DevTools session to find the actual class or attribute used by the star rating widget (common Magento candidates: .rating-summary, .rating-result, [data-bind*="rating"], .product-reviews-summary).
  • **Replace** the invalid 'Star rating widget' selector string in the YAML with a stable CSS selector or XPath derived from the real DOM (e.g. #pdp-info-panel .rating-summary).
  • **Avoid free-text descriptive strings** as selectors — Playwright only accepts valid CSS selectors, XPath expressions, or its own extended syntax (:text(), :has-text(), etc.); a plain label like 'Star rating widget' will never resolve.
  • **Re-run the test** on a PDP URL that has an actual product with reviews/ratings to ensure the element is present in the test data state, as rating widgets may be hidden when a product has zero reviews.
  • If the rating widget is confirmed absent on the live site for products without reviews, consider adding a **hold: true** guard or a precondition that navigates to a product known to have ratings.

  • **Ensure test preconditions are met**: a specific product SKU with store availability data must be in the test setup; an empty/unconfigured product will not show store availability.

#02 Verify visible: Store with Pickup Available Ready in 24 Hours status, Store with This item is currently unavailable at this outlet status The modal should list stores with both pickup available and currently unavailable statuses
⚠ Errorlocator.waitFor: Unexpected token "24" while parsing css selector "Store with Pickup Available Ready in 24 Hours status". Did you mean to CSS.escape it? Call log: [2m - waiting for #store-availability-modal >> Store with Pickup Available Ready in 24 Hours status >> nth=0[22m
🔍 Root Cause
[B] TEST SELECTOR ISSUE — the test is passing a plain text string as a CSS selector, which is syntactically invalid. The selector "Store with Pickup Available Ready in 24 Hours status" is being interpreted as a CSS selector, causing the parser to choke on the numeric token "24". This is a text-based label lookup that must be expressed as an XPath contains(normalize-space(.)) expression or a Playwright text= locator — not a raw CSS string. Additionally, the live page HTML returned empty, which may mean the modal is not yet open when the check runs, but the primary failure is the malformed selector itself.
❌ Problematic Code
# Inside the store availability modal verification step:
selector: "Store with Pickup Available Ready in 24 Hours status"
# ↑ This is raw human-readable text being passed as a CSS selector — invalid.
# CSS parser fails at the token "24" (numeric token in unexpected position).
✅ Fixed Code
# Option 1: XPath text match (most reliable for dynamic text content)
selector: "//*[@id='store-availability-modal']//*[contains(normalize-space(.), 'Ready in 24 Hours')]"

# Option 2: Scoped to the modal with a stable data attribute, if present
selector: "#store-availability-modal [data-status='available']"

# Option 3: If the store row has a class for available status
selector: "#store-availability-modal .store-item.available"

# Option 4: Playwright text locator syntax (if the test runner supports it)
selector: "#store-availability-modal >> text=Ready in 24 Hours"
📋 What To Do
  • **QA Engineer:** Replace the invalid CSS string selector with a proper XPath or text-based locator — e.g. "//*[@id='store-availability-modal']//*[contains(normalize-space(.), 'Ready in 24 Hours')]".
  • **QA Engineer:** Inspect the live modal DOM (open the modal manually in the browser DevTools) to find stable attributes on the store availability rows — look for data-status, data-role, class, or aria-label values that distinguish available vs. unavailable stores.
  • **QA Engineer:** Ensure the test flow actually **triggers the modal to open** before this verification step runs (e.g. click a "Check Store Availability" button first), since the live page HTML was empty — the modal may be hidden/unrendered until triggered.
  • **QA Engineer:** Split the selector into two assertions — one for an available store row and one for an unavailable store row — using separate, stable selectors rather than a single combined text string.
  • **Do NOT** modify website HTML/CSS; this is purely a test YAML selector fix.
